headline: Local IT professional begins charging US companies 'emotional labor fee' for every Zoom call delayed by visa paperwork
body:
"I started by billing them $50 for the silence while I refreshed the visa portal, but now I’ve added a 'psychological stabilization surcharge' just for waking up at 3 AM to join a stand-up meeting," said a Senior Software Engineer based in Bangalore.

"My landlord actually accepted three 'visa-processing-delay' invoices as part of my monthly rent payment, so I suppose the market has spoken on the value of my frustration," noted a perplexed freelance graphic designer.

"The invoice clearly states that if the US company doesn't confirm my H-1B status, they owe me an additional administrative fee for the time I spent explaining to my mother why I’m still not married," explained a junior developer.

"I’ve seen better margins on these fake invoices than I ever did working as a full-time consultant, mostly because the American HR departments just auto-approve anything that looks like a legal government filing fee," laughed a local coffee shop owner who has begun outsourcing his tax filing to frustrated visa applicants.

"I sent a final notice for $200 because the judge’s ruling made me look at a document twice, and frankly, I think I’ve finally found a career path more lucrative than actual coding," added a cloud architect.
caption: Forget the $100,000 fee, the real money is in billing for the anxiety. #VisaFees #TechLife #WorkLifeBalance #H1B (satire)
igHook: Would you pay a 'frustration fee' to your boss if the tables were turned?
imagePrompt: A close-up of a person typing on a laptop in a dimly lit room, with several open browser tabs of legal documents and a half-empty cup of tea nearby.

sourceHeadline.title: Second judge blocks Trump's $100,000 fee for new H-1B worker visas

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 4 stood out for its shift from physical couch fees (a recurring theme in the batch) to the absurd concept of 'emotional labor billing' against corporations. It maintained a deadpan, professional tone while offering a specific, vivid image of a developer billing for the anxiety of 3 AM stand-up meetings, making it the most fresh and grounded entry.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses satirical, archetypal characters to comment on bureaucratic frustrations without naming specific individuals or institutions. The image prompt is generic and avoids identifiable people or copyrighted materials.
